page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 physical cores operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the lower 25% tier, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution leverages the 24 dedicated cores effectively, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth also performs within the average range, reaching 90.83 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 52.97 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the lack of local storage, this instance is structured for compute-bound workloads that scale horizontally across multiple threads rather than those requiring high single-thread performance or massive memory footprints. It is suitable for multi-threaded batch processing, static web serving, and basic database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the utilization of older Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 hardware offers a functional option for legacy x86_64 applications that benefit from dedicated core allocations without requiring modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX.
